_comment: FP64 speed-of-light reference per device, keyed by card slug (card_<slug>.json, cpu_card_<slug>.json). R_SOL = fma_per_s / 22 sample-steps per second (22 = 16 DFMA + 4 DMUL + 2 DADD per step). source: measured (probe), spec (published rate x recorded clock), or pending (an efficiency is refused). aliases map other card stems onto a slug.

nvidia-a100-sxm4-40gb.method: specification: SM count x FP64 FMA per clock per SM for the compute capability (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput) x the highest SM clock recorded across the card's rows
nvidia-a100-sxm4-40gb.evidence: every row of the card ran at or below 1410 MHz, the device's reported maximum SM clock

nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3.method: specification: SM count x FP64 FMA per clock per SM for the compute capability (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput) x the highest SM clock recorded across the card's rows
nvidia-h100-80gb-hbm3.evidence: every row of the card ran at or below 1980 MHz, the device's reported maximum SM clock

nvidia-l4.method: specification: SM count x FP64 FMA per clock per SM for the compute capability (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput) x the highest SM clock recorded across the card's rows
nvidia-l4.evidence: every row of the card ran at or below 2040 MHz, the device's reported maximum SM clock

tesla-t4.method: specification: SM count x FP64 FMA per clock per SM for the compute capability (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput) x the highest SM clock recorded across the card's rows
tesla-t4.evidence: every row of the card ran at or below 1590 MHz, the device's reported maximum SM clock

quadro-p2000.method: specification: SM count x FP64 FMA per clock per SM for the compute capability (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput) x the highest SM clock recorded across the card's rows
quadro-p2000.evidence: 8 SMs x 4 FMA/clk x 1.075 GHz; the card's rows all ran at the 1075 MHz application clock with no throttle reasons

cross_check.method: register-only FP64 FMA chain probe, best sustained rate; 0.2% below the specification, within its timing resolution, so the specification is the reference (a row of the card reaches 1.0006 x the probe value)

amd-epyc-9b45.method: register-only packed FMA chain probe (AVX-512, 12 packed FMA instructions in the binary), 8 threads = physical cores, best sustained rate
amd-epyc-9b45.evidence: 8 threads 5.2972e11 FMA/s (16 threads 5.3119e11: SMT adds nothing); implied 4138 MHz at 16 FMA/clk/core

intel-xeon-platinum-8581c.method: register-only packed FMA chain probe (AVX-512, 12 packed FMA instructions in the binary), 8 threads = physical cores, best sustained rate
intel-xeon-platinum-8581c.evidence: 8 threads 3.8276e11 FMA/s (16 threads 3.7847e11: SMT adds nothing); implied 2990 MHz at 16 FMA/clk/core

amd-epyc-7b13.method: register-only packed FMA chain probe (AVX2), 8 threads = physical cores, best sustained rate
amd-epyc-7b13.evidence: 8 threads 2.2307e11 FMA/s (16 threads 2.2878e11: SMT adds under 3%)

aarch64.method: published Neoverse-V2 rate: 4 x 128-bit FMA pipes = 8 FP64 FMA/clk/core x 8 cores (the card runs at most 8 threads, as on the x86 machines) x 3.0 GHz (clock from the firmware CPU name)
aarch64.evidence: the register-chain probe read 1.03e11 (2.1 FMA/clk/core): 12 chains cannot fill 4 pipes x 4-cycle latency, so it under-measures; the spec rate is the conservative reference

nvidia-rtx-pro-6000-blackwell-server-edi.method: specification: SM count x FP64 FMA per clock per SM for the compute capability (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput) x the highest SM clock recorded across the card's rows
nvidia-rtx-pro-6000-blackwell-server-edi.evidence: 188 SMs x 2 FMA/clk x 2.422 GHz (the card's rows ran at 2317-2422 MHz)

cross_check.method: register-only FP64 FMA chain probe in the card session (dp_sol_probe), best sustained rate at an implied 2426 MHz; 0.2% above the specification at the row clock, so the specification is the reference
